subject: Hosted API: Data locality & retention controls — scenario Q&A
messages:
From: Josh Turner <josh.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API security questionnaire — data locality & retention scenarios

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through a short set of scenario-based questions for our InfoSec review. The attached questionnaire (PDF) has the primary fields, but the three items below are priority for our legal team:

1) If a tenant requests full erasure (right-to-be-forgotten), what is the end-to-end timeline including backups and cache eviction?
2) We need a clear description of where hosted API request payloads and generated outputs may be stored or cached (including logs, analytics, and monitoring).
3) Are there any supported configurations to ensure data never leaves the us-east region (including backups and disaster recovery replicas)?

Can you provide scenario-level answers (short bullets + any caveats)? We may follow up with a call.

Appreciate it,
Josh
Josh Turner
Head of Security Programs — Acme Health

Attachment: acme_questionnaire_initial.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Josh Turner <josh.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-17T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire — data locality & retention scenarios

Hi Josh — thanks for the clear ask. Answering each scenario below; I kept each response short with any operational caveats. Quoting your questions inline for clarity.

---
1) Full erasure / right-to-be-forgotten — timeline and backups:
- Primary store: Tenant data submitted to the hosted API (payloads and generated tokens) are retained in ephemeral request logs for up to 7 days by default; customers can request shorter windows.
- Erasure steps: once we receive a verified erasure request we: (a) mark the tenant records for deletion in the control plane (same day), (b) trigger removal from primary stores (within 48 hours), (c) purge searchable indices and per-tenant caches (48–72 hours), and (d) initiate backup scrub job for any backups containing tenant keys (backup scrub window depends on snapshot cadence; typical commitment: within 30 days).
- Caveats: Restores from older backups could reintroduce data until the scrub job completes. For regulated customers we offer an accelerated purge SLA (contracted) and direct assistance to validate deletion.

2) Where request payloads / outputs may be stored or cached:
- Short-term KV caches and prefix caches on inference nodes: ephemeral (seconds–hours) to optimize latency; these do not persist beyond cache eviction policies.
- Operational logs: request metadata (timestamps, route, token counts) are retained for observability; payloads are redacted by default in logs unless customer elects full payload logging (opt-in).
- Traces/metrics: aggregated telemetry (no PII) retained in metrics backends up to 90 days.
- Long-term archives: we do not persist user payloads in long-term analytics by default; if a customer enables audit logging/payload audit exports we store the exported data in a customer-controlled S3 or supplied endpoint.

3) Region-locking (us-east only) and backups:
- We support config for region-restricted tenancy on hosted API for enterprise customers: primary processing and persistent artifacts are pinned to specified region(s).
- Backups & DR: we can configure snapshots to remain in the same region; by default cross-region replication is disabled for region-locked tenants.
- Caveats: some control-plane metadata (account admin, billing events) may be routed through our control plane services in a separate region unless explicitly contracted for a private control plane.

---
I attached a lightweight data-flow diagram and a retention table for typical defaults and contracted options. Keeping Neha (legal/compliance) copied — she can confirm wording for your procurement group if you want to include this in an SOW.

Next steps: happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd like a run-through.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_data-flow-diagram.png, retention-table.csv

From: compliance@acmehealth.com <compliance@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire — data locality & retention scenarios

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we escalate to procurement: 

A) Emergency purge: if Acme issues an immediate legal hold removal request and we need to prevent any accidental restore from backups, can Redwood place a hold on restores until the scrub completes? Please describe the operational steps and expected maximum window.

B) Monitoring & analytics logs: you mention payload redaction by default. If we elect full payload audit exports (to our S3), will Redwood retain a copy anywhere else? We need to ensure there are no additional internal copies.

Looking for short authoritative answers we can include in our risk register.

— Compliance Team

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: compliance@acmehealth.com <compliance@acmehealth.com>, Josh Turner <josh.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire — data locality & retention scenarios

Hi — Neha from Legal & Product Ops here. Quick, authoritative responses inline.

A) Emergency purge / hold on restores:
- Yes. For enterprise / contracted tenants we operate a coordinated restore-blocking mechanism: upon a verified emergency purge request we suspend inbound restore operations for that tenant and mark all snapshots referencing tenant identifiers as "pending scrub."
- Operational steps: (1) issue verified request through our secure portal or signed SOW, (2) we suspend restore capability for tenant ID within 2 business hours, (3) kick off backup scrub job which removes tenant keys/segments from snapshot index (target completion: 30 days for standard cadence; accelerated scrub available as a contracted option that can often complete within 7–14 days depending on snapshot size).
- Maximum window: standard backup retention policies are driven by snapshot cadence; we commit to prevent any manual or automated restore for the tenant as soon as the restore suspension is in place.

B) Payload audit exports to customer S3:
- If Acme configures export of payloads/audit logs to your S3 bucket, Redwood will not retain an independent long-term copy beyond transient staging during transfer (staging TTL <24 hours).
- We do keep short-lived transfer logs (transfer success/failure metadata) for troubleshooting and they do not contain full payloads.
- If a customer requests archival on Redwood-managed storage, that would be documented and controlled under the SOW — otherwise the only long-term export resides in your S3.

If helpful, we can provide a brief addendum clause for your procurement that codifies restore suspension and accelerated scrub SLAs. Ben — I included you for sales visibility on potential contract addendum.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal & Compliance — Redwood Inference
